title: Exodus Bible Quiz - Chapter 15
description: Ten questions on Exodus 15: the song by the sea, Miriam's tambourine and the waters of Marah and Elim.

questions.text: Who sang the song to Yahweh after the crossing of the sea?
questions.explanation: Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to Yahweh.

answers.text: Moses and the children of Israel

questions.text: What does the song say Yahweh has thrown into the sea?
questions.explanation: The song begins: 'He has thrown the horse and his rider into the sea.'

questions.text: What does the song call Yahweh in verse 3?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says: 'Yahweh is a man of war. Yahweh is his name.'

questions.text: According to verse 10, the enemies sank like what in the mighty waters?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says: 'You blew with your wind. The sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.'

questions.text: Pangs took hold of the inhabitants of which land?
questions.explanation: The song says the peoples heard and trembled, and pangs took hold of the inhabitants of Philistia.

questions.text: How is Miriam the prophetess described?
questions.explanation: Miriam the prophetess is called the sister of Aaron.

questions.text: What did Miriam take in her hand?
questions.explanation: Miriam took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and with dances.

questions.text: How long did they go in the wilderness of Shur without finding water?
questions.explanation: They went three days in the wilderness of Shur and found no water.

questions.text: What did Yahweh show Moses to make the waters of Marah sweet?
questions.explanation: Yahweh showed him a tree; he threw it into the waters, and the waters were made sweet.

questions.text: What did they find at Elim?
questions.explanation: At Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they encamped there by the waters.

answers.text: Twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees
Three springs and forty palm trees
One deep well and a field of grain
A river and many fig trees
